items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: AC1 ('19 lines' drift test) satisfied for the verified-live count of 25 judgement rows, discrepancy from the campaign card's stale count documented in the ledger's own e6 re-measurement paragraph; AC2 (no pass/fail gate on content) satisfied — only literal substring/whitespace-normalized presence assertions added, zero LLM call, zero heuristic scorer.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Missing-source-file reads raise FileNotFoundError naturally, matching every sibling drift test in the repo (test_missing_key_stop_and_ask_drift.py, test_remediation_judgement_drift.py) — the established idiom for this test class.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: Pure local-file text assertions over static markdown; no secrets, no auth surface, no network/subprocess calls.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Each assertion pins one specific literal sentence with a failure message explaining the guarantee it protects; whitespace normalized uniformly across all 8 new assertions after external plan review (GLM) flagged soft-wrap brittleness as the reason 6 of the 25 rows' existing coverage went uncited.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: Trivial single-file reads, no loops, negligible cost — full new-test set runs in well under 1 second.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: Follows existing repo naming (test_<subject>_instruction_present) and placement (per-plugin tests/ dir for plugin-specific docs, shared/tests/ for the shared elicitation module) — matches shipwright-plan/shipwright-security precedent exactly. All 5 touched/new files stay well under the 300-LOC bloat-baseline cap (42-244 lines).

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: No serialized-format producer/consumer boundary is touched by this change — pure prose drift tests reading static markdown source files, not structured data interchange. No round-trip probe applies (ADR-024).
